The list should look like this: 2020/11111, 2020/11112, 2020/11115, 2020/11116, 2020/11117, 2020/11119, 2020/11125

I’m sorry, but I wasn’t able to locate a definitive list of PRA numbers that meet all of the criteria you specified. The Product Safety website’s recall catalogue can only be accessed through its front‑end search interface, and that interface – and the database that powers it – is not easily scraped by automated search tools. Because of that limitation, I couldn’t pull a clean, filtered list of every recall published from 1 January 2020 to 1 July 2020 that is tagged “Gas products and appliances” and sold nationally.

**What you can do next**

| Step | How to do it |
|------|--------------|
| 1 | **Go to the recalls page** – <https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls> |
| 2 | **Use the web‑interface “Search”**.  In the “Topic” drop‑down, choose “Gas products and appliances”.  Leave the “Country” filter set to “Australia” (this defaults to nationally sold). |
| 3 | **Filter the date range**.  The site does not have a built‑in date picker for the publish date, but you can read the “Published” date that is shown on each recall card.  Filter visually or look for those dated between 01‑Jan‑2020 and 31‑Mar‑2020 (the earliest recall after 1 January 2020 will be naturally around that time). |
| 4 | **Collect the PRA numbers**.  They appear in the header of each recall page (e.g., “PRA no. 2020/11112”).  Either take a screenshot or copy the text. |
| 5 | **Compile**.  Put the numbers in one line separated by commas, just as you requested: `2020/11112, 2020/11543, …` . |

If you want a fully automated solution, you could write a short script that:

1. Uses Selenium or Playwright to open the recalls page.  
2. Selects “Gas products and appliances” from the topic filter.  
3. Loops through the resulting list, clicking each card, reading the publish date, and saving the PRA number if the date falls in the desired window and the “Country sold” (often displayed as “Sold in Australia”) is present.

This will give you an exact, up‑to‑date list without missing any recalls.

I hope this helps you locate the precise set of recall numbers you need for your study. If you run into any specific issues while crawling the site, feel free to let me know and I can help troubleshoot the script.

I’m sorry, but I wasn’t able to locate a definitive list of PRA numbers that meet all of the criteria you specified. The Product Safety website’s recall catalogue can only be accessed through its front‑end search interface, and that interface – and the database that powers it – is not easily scraped by automated search tools. Because of that limitation, I couldn’t pull a clean, filtered list of every recall published from 1 January 2020 to 1 July 2020 that is tagged “Gas products and appliances” and sold nationally.

**What you can do next**

| Step | How to do it |
|------|--------------|
| 1 | **Go to the recalls page** – <https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls> |
| 2 | **Use the web‑interface “Search”**.  In the “Topic” drop‑down, choose “Gas products and appliances”.  Leave the “Country” filter set to “Australia” (this defaults to nationally sold). |
| 3 | **Filter the date range**.  The site does not have a built‑in date picker for the publish date, but you can read the “Published” date that is shown on each recall card.  Filter visually or look for those dated between 01‑Jan‑2020 and 31‑Mar‑2020 (the earliest recall after 1 January 2020 will be naturally around that time). |
| 4 | **Collect the PRA numbers**.  They appear in the header of each recall page (e.g., “PRA no. 2020/11112”).  Either take a screenshot or copy the text. |
| 5 | **Compile**.  Put the numbers in one line separated by commas, just as you requested: `2020/11112, 2020/11543, …` . |

If you want a fully automated solution, you could write a short script that:

1. Uses Selenium or Playwright to open the recalls page.  
2. Selects “Gas products and appliances” from the topic filter.  
3. Loops through the resulting list, clicking each card, reading the publish date, and saving the PRA number if the date falls in the desired window and the “Country sold” (often displayed as “Sold in Australia”) is present.

This will give you an exact, up‑to‑date list without missing any recalls.
